correctness.rationale: The full complex matrix-unit equations have the stated permutation-trivial and standard blocks. To see that they exhaust the non-scalar action, the off-diagonal leaf row/column-sum map has image the pairs of vectors with equal total sum. On mean-zero coefficient vectors its 2×2 map is [[n−1,−1],[−1,n−1]], invertible for n≥3; the constant off-diagonal block supplies the common scalar sum. Its kernel is precisely the zero-diagonal leaf-only remainder of dimension n²−3n+1. In a standard block the sum of the two hub–leaf coordinates and difference of the off-diagonal coordinates form the quadratic sector; the complementary three variables give S_n. In the trivial block the trace is conserved and the symmetric hub–leaf variable decays at −γ, leaving the T_n sector. The factors, multiplicities, and simple zero follow. In the positive-u parametrization y=2u/(u²+1−2/n), γ is strictly increasing onto (0,∞) since y′≥−1/[4(1−2/n)]. This gives the unique root in the stated interval and the unique optimizer. After shifting by −s, S_n reduces to w times a strictly stable quadratic. For shifted T_n, a=2γ−3s>0, c_T=a ng², and b_T>ng², so Routh–Hurwitz gives strict separation; the other factors lie at real part −γ. The contrast is the diagonal coefficient in the standard three-variable block with initial value 1, giving the stated numerator, positive residue, and observed rate. The sentence at line 120 calling s itself an eigenvalue is a sign slip: it is −s, as the shifted proof and finding require. Independent direct matrix-unit generation gave exact polynomial agreement at (n,g,γ)=(3,−2,7),(4,1,2),(5,2,9) and exact rational leaf-resolvent agreement at z=1,3 in each case; these finite checks support, not replace, the proof.
residual_risks: Only homogeneous positive site dephasing with nonzero real adjacency coupling is covered. The theorem is about long-time relaxation, not an optimal finite-time mixing threshold.

evidence: The coherent star papers study Hamiltonian evolution or adjacency spectral distributions without the dissipator. Bressanini et al. use same-site Haken–Strobl projectors but a Laplacian Hamiltonian and fidelity distance. The network preprint proves uniqueness of the maximally mixed state under irreducibility and fits noisy relaxation. The exact lossy-star and complete-bipartite absorption findings measure killing times with a central/part sink.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Coherent spectra, stationary-state uniqueness, fitted relaxations and mean absorption from a lossy generator do not imply the full nonzero spectrum of a trace-preserving adjacency-star Liouvillian or the leaf-sector ordering.

evidence: The universal-hub result at unit hopping has a normalized contrast numerator (z+γ)²+N²−2N and denominator z[(z+γ)²+N²]+2Nγ, where N is the number of sites. Choosing the complete graph makes its Laplacian NI−J; the identity term drops out of the commutator. The normalized hub excess is the hub population minus any other population by symmetry.
Other indexed star optimizers use a sink; the published no-sink noisy-star comparison uses the graph Laplacian, which on a star is not adjacency plus a scalar or an overall sign.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Set N=n and rescale time by α=|g|/√n with original dephasing γ/α; the complete-graph Laplace transform then has numerator (z+γ)²+(n−2)g² and denominator S_n exactly. This proves equivalence of the functions, not of the physical systems or their full spectra. At the same leaf count a Laplacian-star hub trajectory is a different specialization and cannot identify the adjacency-star leaf-difference spectral multiplicities.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the exhaustive all-n adjacency-star Liouvillian factorization and the strict comparison showing that its standard sector dominates all additional star sectors. An earlier-dated universal-hub indexed result, specialized to a complete graph and rescaled, already gives the same rational scalar transfer function, including its numerator and S_n denominator. This is stronger overlap than identifying the cubic alone. The scalar contrast law and optimum of its dominant rate are not independent novelty claims; the new content is that this mode is realized by a leaf contrast in the adjacency star and governs the entire star relaxation despite additional sectors. None of the inspected sources gives or forces this complete star-specific result.
residual_risks: The frozen text does not identify the specific full complete-graph spectral antecedent it mentions. Exact equivalence of its observed transfer is established here from a located source; no claim is made as to who first derived it.
An uninspected more general operator-spectrum theorem could cover the remaining adjacency-star factorization. The searches and inspected material are bounded.

value.rationale: The all-order reduction resolves a growing nonnormal generator into fixed low-degree spectral factors and quantifies multiplicities and separation. For a canonical hub–leaf system it identifies a measurable contrast that sees the actual global relaxation exponent, rather than just a fitted decay or absorption rate. The full spectral comparison carries this value even though a rescaled scalar transfer was already known.
residual_risks: No inference is made about optimal mixing for other observables, nonuniform dephasing, or arbitrary networks.
